The season started on 16 August 2024 and ended on 25 June 2025.{{cite web |date=9 August 2024 |title=RATIBA YA LIGI KUU YA NBC MSIMU WA 2024/2025 |url=https://ligikuu.co.tz/ratiba-ya-ligi-kuu-ya-nbc-msimu-wa-2024-2025/ |access-date=2024-08-16 |language=sw}} The [[Young Africans]] drew the highest average home league attendance with 10,176. ==Teams== The league consisted of 16 teams; the top 14 teams from the previous season, and two teams promoted from the [[Tanzanian Championship League]]. [[Young Africans S.C.|Young Africans]] entered the season as defending champions (for the third consecutive season).{{cite web |date=15 August 2024 |title=Yanga target domestic glory and deeper CAF Champions League run this season |url=https://www.ippmedia.com/the-guardian/sports/football/read/yanga-target-domestic-glory-and-deeper-caf-champions-league-run-this-season-2024-08-14-165242 |access-date=2024-08-16 |language=en-US}} The promoted teams were the 2023–24 Tanzanian Championship League champions KenGold and runners-up [[Pamba S.C.|Pamba Jiji]]. They replaced the [[2023–24 Tanzanian Premier League]] bottom two teams Geita Gold and [[Mtibwa Sugar F.C.|Mtibwa Sugar]]. === Name changes === * Before the start of the season, Ihefu FC renamed their club as the Singida Black Stars as part of a rebrand.{{cite web |date=11 August 2024 |title=Confirmed: Club name change, not a transfer – Super Eagles defender remains as Ihefu FC becomes Singida Black Stars |url=https://soccernet.ng/2024/08/confirmed-club-name-change-not-a-transfer-super-eagles-defender-remains-as-ihefu-fc-becomes-singida-black-stars.html |access-date=2024-08-16 |language=en-US}} ===Locations=== {{Location map+|Tanzania|width=500 |float=center|caption=Location of clubs in Tanzania for the 2024–25 Tanzanian Premier League season |places= {{Location map~|Tanzania||lat=-02.50 |long=32.90|label='''[[Pamba S.C.|Pamba Jiji]]''' |position=top|mark=Red pog.svg}} {{Location map~|Tanzania||lat=-06.81 |long=39.27|label='''[[Simba Sports Club|Simba]]'''

Held over two legs, the Championship teams qualified for the quarter-finals, followed by the Premier League teams facing each other in the semi-finals and the winners remaining in the league; the quarter-final winners then faced the semi-final losers for the final place in the 2025–26 Tanzanian Premier League. === Quarter-finals === ==== First leg ==== {{football box collapsible |date = 24 May
